clue.text: Pull back jemmy, perhaps to get this?

definitions.text: Pull back jemmy, perhaps to get this?

indicators.note: pulling something back draws it the opposite way, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a jemmy is an example of a burglar's tool, a short crowbar

explanation.surface: A burglar levers open a window with a crowbar in the hope of grabbing something worth taking.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: what a burglar wielding a jemmy is after is LOOT, and 'pull back' also describes levering with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot is stolen goods, the haul a burglar hopes to carry away after forcing entry.

clue.text: Fifty humming Romanies holding fine tune

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: holding means wrapping around another piece, so one letter sits inside the rearranged group
humming suggests something busily buzzing about, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A band of travellers hums a pleasant melody together.
explanation.walkthrough: Fine qualifies tune in the surface, but it is the single letter F lodged after the first letter of the rearranged Romanies.
explanation.definitionFit: Life on Mars? is a 1971 David Bowie song, so it is an example of a tune.

clue.text: Briefly inform warrant officer about new hooter?

indicators.note: briefly means cutting a word short, so its final letter is lopped off
about here means turned around, so the combined letters are read backwards in this down entry

parts.note: tell, meaning inform, without its last letter
WO is the military abbreviation for warrant officer

explanation.surface: Someone is told to tip off a sergeant-major about a new nose.
explanation.walkthrough: Hooter is slang for a nose, but here it is literally something that hoots, an owl; a young one is an OWLET.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a baby owl, and owls are birds that hoot, so a fledgling one is a new hooter.

clue.text: A film actor in pieces centred on the mum

indicators.note: something in pieces has been broken up, so these letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A screen performer falls apart emotionally in a story all about his mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Matrifocal describes a family or society organised around the mother as its central figure.

clue.text: When guards ask opinion over striking lads

indicators.note: guards means surrounds protectively, so one word sits around the others

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
to poll is to canvass people's views
O is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Guards on duty ask what people think about some lads who have gone on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: Striking means good-looking, not walking out; the plural noun fits a plural definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An Apollo is a handsome young man, after the beautiful Greek god, so Apollos are good-looking youths.

clue.text: Is reluctant concerning relative boxing in street

parts.note: re means concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: boxing in means enclosing, so one short word is held inside another

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a relative
St is the address abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates about a family member who is trapping them in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to hold back or push against, the behaviour of someone unwilling to go along.

clue.text: Daft American cop describing what zombie may do to girl?

indicators.note: describing in the sense of drawing a line around, so one word surrounds the phrase

parts.note: a fed is a US federal agent
zombies are said to eat brains
her stands for any girl
the object of the zombie's eating, the girl's brain

explanation.surface: A dim US policeman describes a horror-film scene of a zombie attacking a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Fed is American slang for an FBI agent. The surface reads 'describing' as telling a story, but it means drawing a line around the zombie's meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Feather-brained means silly and empty-headed, as if one's skull held only feathers.

clue.text: My stripped-down play worried United

indicators.note: stripped down means stripped of its outer layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise like 'my!'
sport, meaning play, without its outer letters
ate means worried, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: A fan exclaims that a dull performance has left Manchester United anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: United looks like a football club but is the definition. Cor is a British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporate means combined into one body or shared by a group, so it is a synonym of joined together.

clue.text: Dirty spring coming up short on depth

indicators.note: short means lacking its end, so the last letter is dropped
in a down entry, coming up means rising from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: well, a spring of water, missing its last letter
D is the standard abbreviation for depth

explanation.surface: A muddy spring bubbles up but is too shallow.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty in the sense of smutty or obscene, which is exactly what lewd means.

clue.text: Certain produce nobbled and not returned

indicators.note: something nobbled has been tampered with, so the letters are interfered with and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Some goods have been tampered with and the seller refuses to take them back.
explanation.walkthrough: Not returned suggests goods kept, but it means feelings not given back in kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreciprocated love or favours are ones the other person does not give back in return.

clue.text: Criminal chap with joint setters reported

indicators.note: reported means said out loud, so the result is how the words sound when spoken

parts.note: a fellow is a chap
the knee is a joint of the leg
crossword setters refer to themselves as us

explanation.surface: A man and his fellow crossword compilers are said to be crooks.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'fellow knee us' runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Felonious means relating to felony, serious crime, so it is a synonym of the adjective criminal.

clue.text: Pointer one wouldn't want to take to heart?

definitions.text: Pointer one wouldn't want to take to heart?

parts.note: surface reading: a hint or tip one would rather not take seriously

parts.words: one wouldn't want to take to heart
parts.note: setter's reading: a pointed missile that nobody wants lodged in their chest

explanation.walkthrough: To take advice to heart is to heed it; read literally, the heart is where the pointed projectile would strike, unless Cupid fired it.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a pointing sign and also a shaft fired from a bow, which could pierce someone's chest.

clue.text: Traditional food loch hotels reinvented

indicators.note: reinvented means remade in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Classic Scottish lakeside hotels have given their menus a modern makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the old school is an idiom for old-fashioned, holding to customary ways.

clue.text: Business complaint of long-standing croupier?

parts.note: a croupier is a casino dealer, and 'of' makes it possessive
a hip complaint, the ailment of someone who stands for long hours

explanation.surface: A casino dealer who stands all shift develops a bad joint.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as dealer's hip, the ailment a croupier on their feet all night might get; long-standing is a joke, not a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealership is a franchised business selling a maker's goods, such as cars.

clue.text: Shape cut by small glacial ice shafts

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: mould, meaning shape, with its final letter removed
by and in are interchangeable in 'drop by' and 'drop in'
S is the clothing abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Little vertical tunnels in a glacier are carved into shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A moulin is a vertical shaft in a glacier down which meltwater pours, from the French for mill.

clue.text: Rub this in after running, not cricket!

indicators.note: after running the letters have been set in motion and land in another order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Gloating over a beaten opponent after a race is poor sportsmanship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not cricket' is a British idiom for unsporting or unfair behaviour, which the stereotype holds to be foreign to the national character.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair conduct is jokingly called un-British because fair play is supposedly a national virtue.

clue.text: Riseof brilliant sportsperson on board

definitions.note: the source runs 'Rise of' together; Rise is the definition and of is a link word

parts.note: to surf is to ride the waves on a board
an ace is a star performer

explanation.surface: A top athlete is promoted to the club's board of directors.
explanation.walkthrough: The source runs 'Rise' and 'of' together as 'Riseof'. Read as surf ace, a champion surfer is a star on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: To surface is to rise to the top of water, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Are you (through wine) kind of lippy?

parts.note: text-message shorthand, R and U
by means through, as in 'by means of'
red is a wine

explanation.surface: Someone is asked if they are chatty after a few drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Lippy here is not cheeky but British slang for lipstick.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby-red is a deep shade of lipstick, so it describes one type of lippy.

clue.text: Run out of brut? Very bad show

indicators.note: run out of means the letter for a run is taken out of the word

parts.note: brut describes dry champagne; dry with R, cricket's run, removed
nasty means very bad

explanation.surface: A party running short of champagne is a dreadful affair.
explanation.walkthrough: Brut is the label for the driest champagne. R for run is the cricket scorebook abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynasty was a 1980s American soap opera, so it is an example of a TV show.

clue.text: Serious Republican about to load Colt?

indicators.note: to load something is to put it inside, so these letters are packed into the other word

parts.note: a colt is a young horse, a foal
R is the abbreviation for Republican
re means about

explanation.surface: A US politician considers loading a Colt revolver.
explanation.walkthrough: Colt reads as the gun brand but is just a young horse.
explanation.definitionFit: For real is an informal idiom meaning genuine or in earnest.

clue.text: Gear aboard large eastern vessel

indicators.note: aboard means inside, so one word goes within the others

parts.note: fat means large
rig is equipment or gear
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: Equipment is loaded onto a big ship from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: A frigate is a type of warship, so it is an example of a vessel.

clue.text: Cooler product found in East End salon?

indicators.note: East End speakers traditionally drop the H at the start of a word

parts.note: a product found in a hairdresser's
surface padding: the salon is where the hair product is found

explanation.surface: A cooling gadget turns up in a Cockney hairdresser's.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End of London is home to the Cockney accent, famous for dropping H; a salon's product said there loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An air conditioner is a machine that cools a room, so it is a cooler.

clue.text: Perhaps Smash Hits magazine's last report?

parts.note: smash hits are, for example, number ones, No 1s

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of magazine

explanation.surface: A query whether a review appeared in the closing pages of a pop magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Smash Hits was a British pop magazine, but here it means chart-topping records, written No 1s with the digit as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a loud bang, such as a gunshot, so it is a kind of noise.

clue.text: Spiritual trip experienced on joints primarily

parts.note: had means experienced, as in 'had a good time'

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of joints

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a trippy experience fuelled by cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: Joints and trip suggest drugs; the trip is a pilgrimage.
explanation.definitionFit: The hadj, or hajj, is the Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca, a religious journey.

clue.text: Idealistic nurses of the highest class?

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the word is carried inside the clue word

parts.note: the run of letters inside this word

explanation.surface: An idealistic person cares for the sick of the highest social class.
explanation.definitionFit: A-list means top-tier, the most sought-after celebrities, used as an adjective for the elite.

clue.text: Swimmer passed if swimming hard

indicators.note: swimming means moving about freely, so the letters float into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A competitor gets through a heat if they swim hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A spadefish is a deep-bodied sea fish, so it is an example of a swimmer.

clue.text: Boring parts can haunt glorious poet

indicators.note: parts means separates, so one piece comes between the two others

parts.note: can and john are both slang for a toilet
dry means dull or boring
a den is a favourite haunt

explanation.surface: Dull bits of a tin might be haunted by a magnificent poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Scott and others called the poet 'Glorious John', which explains the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was the English Restoration poet and first official Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Sudden surge in energy-consuming circuit

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing up, so one letter sits inside another word

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sudden spike in energy use in an electrical circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A leap is a sharp jump or increase, as in a leap in prices.
